# OpenCode Mobile — Full Documentation & System Context

> OpenCode Mobile is an unofficial, self-hosted mobile, tablet, and web client for the OpenCode AI coding agent. It connects directly to your development workstation with 1-command setup, terminal ANSI QR pairing, a universal model selector (DeepSeek, Claude 3.7, Gemini 4 Argon, OpenAI, Ollama), a Claude-inspired 120fps fluid UI, and zero telemetry.

Version: 1.0.0-beta.10  
Repository: https://github.com/Aetherdz/opencode-mobile  
Website: https://aetherdz.github.io/opencode-mobile/  
Latest Release APK: https://github.com/Aetherdz/opencode-mobile/releases/download/v1.0.0-beta.10/opencode-mobile-1.0.0-beta.10.apk  

---

## 1. Quick Installation & Pairing

### Linux & macOS (Automated)
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aetherdz/opencode-mobile-dist/main/install.sh | bash
```

### Windows (Automated PowerShell)
```powershell
$h = "3a493282e252468ed96012cd0019f5252314bfb5c7b810be34476602616a14aa"
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aetherdz/opencode-mobile-dist/7c4ec38b7de7d87e88d7f215721a11bc338e128f/install.ps1 -OutFile install.ps1
if ((Get-FileHash .\install.ps1 -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $h) { throw "checksum mismatch" }
.\install.ps1 -Command install -WorkDir "$env:USERPROFILE\projects"
```

### Pairing with Mobile App
1. Run `opencode-mobile` in your terminal on the workstation.
2. The CLI generates an ANSI terminal QR code containing the pairing URL (`opencode-mobile://connect?url=...&token=...`).
3. Open OpenCode Mobile on your phone and tap **Auto-Connect (QR Scan)** or paste from clipboard.
4. The app verifies credentials, establishes a secure WebSocket connection, and lists your sessions.

---

## 2. Architecture & Transport Engine

OpenCode Mobile operates around a defense-in-depth model that connects your mobile device directly to your workstation without third-party intermediary servers:

```text
[Mobile App / PWA] 
       │
       ▼ (Encrypted WireGuard / HTTPS / LAN)
[Fastify Bridge @ 127.0.0.1:8787]
  • Bearer Token Authentication (crypto.timingSafeEqual)
  • Scoped Confinement (ALLOWED_WORKDIRS = ~/projects)
  • Magic-byte verification & upload limits
  • Dual Transport: Primary WebSocket (/ws) + SSE Fallback (/event)
       │
       ▼ (Loopback HTTP REST + SSE)
[OpenCode Local Core @ 127.0.0.1]
  • Discovered via ~/.local/state/opencode/service.json
  • Tool execution (bash, edit, read, web)
  • LLM Providers (DeepSeek, Claude 3.7, Gemini 4 Argon, OpenAI, Ollama)
```

### Key Architectural Capabilities
- **Dual-Transport Streaming**: High-frequency primary WebSocket connection (`/ws`) delivering sub-50ms message latency, heartbeat keepalive ping/pong, and automatic fallback to Server-Sent Events (SSE).
- **Universal Model Selector**: Switch seamlessly between any model configured in OpenCode directly in the composer:
  - Gemini 4 Argon (`antigravity-gemini-4-argon`)
  - DeepSeek V3 / R1 (`deepseek/deepseek-chat`, `deepseek/deepseek-reasoner`)
  - Anthropic Claude (`anthropic/claude-3-7-sonnet-latest`, `claude-3-5-sonnet`)
  - OpenAI (`openai/gpt-4o`, `o3-mini`)
  - Local Ollama instances (`ollama/...`)
- **120fps Fluid Mobile UI**: Native fluid physics (`cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`), tactile `PressableScale` spring interactions, interactive tool cards, and dark/light modes.
- **Approvals & Diffs**: Interactive approval sheets for tool permissions with collapsible diff reviews and double confirmation for destructive actions.

---

## 3. Bridge Configuration & Environment Variables

All settings are configured via `bridge/.env`:

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AUTH_TOKEN` | *required* | High-entropy bearer secret (minimum 32 characters). Tested via constant-time comparison. |
| `HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Local IP bind address. Always keep on loopback. |
| `PORT` | `8787` | HTTP & WebSocket server port. |
| `ALLOWED_WORKDIRS` | `~/projects` | Colon-separated directory allowlist for workspace confinement. Prevents path traversal. |
| `OPENCODE_URL` | Auto-discovered | Loopback URL of local OpenCode daemon (from service.json). |
| `OPENCODE_PASSWORD`| Auto-discovered | Local OpenCode authentication secret. |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | *empty* | Exact browser origins permitted for web client (e.g. `http://localhost:8081`). Wildcards rejected. |
| `MAX_UPLOAD_MB` | `25` | Maximum upload size per individual attachment file. |
| `MAX_SESSION_UPLOAD_MB` | `1024` | Cumulative upload limit per session. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `180` | IP-based unauthenticated request rate limit. |

---

## 4. Security & Isolation Specification

- **Loopback Enforcement**: The bridge binds exclusively to `127.0.0.1`. Remote access is routed via end-to-end encrypted networks (Tailscale WireGuard mesh or authenticated reverse proxies).
- **Constant-Time Authentication**: Uses `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for bearer token validation to prevent timing side-channel attacks.
- **One-Time WebSocket Tickets**: Token credentials never appear in WebSocket URLs or access logs. The app requests a 30-second ticket that is consumed upon handshake.
- **Directory Traversal Prevention**: All file paths are strictly resolved against `ALLOWED_WORKDIRS`. Any traversal escape (`../`) is immediately rejected. Out-of-bounds sessions require explicit 1-tap runtime grants.
- **Strict File Upload Validation**: Uploads verify declared MIME types against binary magic bytes (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, PDF) and reject executable extensions.
- **Zero Telemetry Guarantee**: No tracking libraries, no Firebase analytics, no external crash reporting.

## 6. Common Troubleshooting

1. **`ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8787`**: Ensure the bridge service is running (`cd bridge && npm start` or `systemctl --user status opencode-mobile-bridge`).
2. **OpenCode Core Not Found**: Run `opencode service start` to ensure the local OpenCode core is running on loopback.
3. **Session Outside Workdir**: The session directory is outside `ALLOWED_WORKDIRS`. Tap "Authorize Once" on the mobile dialog to grant runtime access.
4. **WebSocket Handshake 401**: Verify that the authentication token is configured properly in the mobile client or re-scan the terminal QR code.
